chapter_theme: Seeing the guru's matha (குருமட தரிசனம்): those who see the guru's seat, where all offerings are understood as the Lord's, reach his feet; and the matha is turned inward, so that the Lord's only house is the person, and the seat, mountain, cave and forest of the yogi are found in the body's centres and the inward-turned face.
structure_note: 2649 to 2651 speak of the matha and the Lord's dwelling; 2652 announces a teaching on the seat, mountain, cave, centres and forest, which 2653 and 2654 give as inner correspondences; 2655 ends with the silent knowers who see the supreme light in their own form.

2649.reading: Those who have seen the guru's matha, where people gather knowing that the offerings, the oblations, the spreading smoke and the sounds are all for the Lord, went on and stood joined to his feet, tender as young leaves and flowers.
2649.nuance: பலி, அவி, புகை and ஒலி are the offerings, oblations, incense and chanting of ritual worship; the matha is valued because there they are known to be the Lord's. குவியும் may be the gathering of people or the folding of hands and minds.

2650.reading: Apart from this one's house he has no house there; if one asks whether he has some other house, they know again and again that this one's house is his, and yet they wail that he is outside.
2650.nuance: அவன் is the Lord and இவன் the person; இல்லம் (house) is usually read as the body or the heart. Line 2 can also be a statement: if one knows, he has no other house.

2651.reading: After I found the great ford that all seek, Siva's red feet, like freshly picked flowers, come to me; our Lord, hard to search out, who has no special mark, stands as the life of the moving world.
2651.nuance: பெருந்துறை (the great ford) may be the shrine of Tirupperunturai or a figure for the place of crossing, the guru or his matha; the verse doesn't settle it. சிறப்பிலி may mean the one without distinguishing marks or without equal.

2652.reading: I will tell of the seat and the mountain, of the cave of the mind and the place, of the centres and the forest, to the people of the twelve great lands.
2652.nuance: The places a yogi might seek outside (seat, mountain, cave, forest) are matched with inner ones (சித்தக் குகை, ஆதாரம்). ஈராறு இருநிலத்தோர் may be the people of the twelve lands, the wide earth, or those at the twelfth centre above the head; it can't be fixed.

2653.reading: The face is the seat, the great matha and the land one seeks; the inner self is the supreme order and the faultless vision; the inner self is the supreme seat and the sixty-four rites; Chidambaram, the cave of the self, is the centre itself.
2653.nuance: Each outward thing of a matha (its seat, building, land, rites) is set equal to something in the person. எண்எண் கிரியை may be sixty-four rites or eight-and-eight. சிதம்பரம் is both the shrine and, by its meaning 'space of consciousness', the inner space; தற்குகை is the cave of the self.

2654.reading: For the knowing who have examined the inward face, the inward face is the seat and the centre; the world-ward face is Shakti's seat; and the face toward the world, the deity, is Siva.
2654.nuance: The verse plays on அகமுகம் (face turned inward), சகமுகம் and செகமுகம் (both read as face turned to the world, from ஜகம்); the difference between the second and third is unclear and one may be a variant. The general sense is that the inward turn is the true seat.

2655.reading: When the two mayas veil and are themselves veiled, and the five bodies pass away and one becomes oneself, and the pure supreme flame appears, those who search within their own form are the silent ones who begin from knowledge.
2655.nuance: மாயை இரண்டும் are traditionally pure and impure maya; காயம் ஓர் ஐந்தும் may be the five sheaths or the five bodies of Siddhanta. ஞானாதி மோனத்தர் may be 'silent ones with knowledge first' or 'silent ones of knowledge and the rest'.

links.note: 2649 says those who have seen the guru's matha (குருமடம் கண்டவர்), where the offerings, smoke and sounds are known to be the Lord's, go on to stand at his feet. 2148 says those who do not know the life within the body wander bewildered like a dog that has strayed into a matha (மடம்புகு நாய்போல் மயங்குகின்றாரே). The same building yields the feet to the one who knows what is done there and only confusion to the one who does not.

2650 says the Lord has no house but this one's house (இவன்இல்லம் அல்லது அவனுக்கு அங்கு இல்லை), yet people who know it still wail that he is outside. 725 tells how the poet came to see that the Highest had made the body his temple (உடம்புளே உத்தமன் கோயில்கொண்டான்) and so cherishes it. 725 is the turn of mind that the people of 2650 know about but never make.

2653 sets each thing of a matha within the person and ends: Chidambaram, the cave of the self, is the centre (சிதம்பரம் தற்குகை ஆதாரம் தானே). 1726 says outright that the form of the human body is Chidambaram (மானுடர் ஆக்கை வடிவு சிதம்பரம்), as it is the linga and the dance. The two place the shrine in the body; 2653 adds the matha's seat and rites to the list.

2655 says that when the two mayas are veiled and the five bodies pass, those who search within their own form are silent ones who begin from knowledge (ஞானாதி மோனத்தர்). 1674 says the Siva-gnani who reaches the state through knowledge is released and a siddha because he is one of silence (மோனத்தன் ஆதலின் முத்தனாம்). 1674 states as a rule what 2655 describes as an outcome: knowledge leads into silence, and silence is release.
